beatOutlines.textOutline: Monday afternoon, Nifty drops 2% from the open and Raju panics.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju thinks every small dip means a major market crash.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji reminds him of a century-old principle: Dow Theory.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Sold at the bottom of a dip
scenes.concept: Sold at the bottom of a dip

beatOutlines.textOutline: Over forty days, Bharat Motors rose from ₹400 to ₹520.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Then in three weeks it pulled back to ₹480, and Raju sold in fear.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: But this was just a one-third retracement before hitting a new high of ₹580.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

takeaways: Sold at the bottom of a dip

beatOutlines.textOutline: In 1884, Charles Dow created the very first stock market barometer.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: He compared market movements to ocean tides, waves, and ripples.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And showed how every major trend passes through three psychological phases.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: On July 3, 1884, Charles Dow published the first stock average of 11 companies.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In 1896 it split into two: Industrials that make goods and Rails that ship them.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dow never wrote a book; after his death, Nelson, Hamilton, and Rhea formalized Dow Theory.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dow's second tenet states that three market trends operate simultaneously.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The Primary trend is the ocean tide lasting years; the Secondary is a 3-week to 3-month wave.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And Minor trends are ripples under three weeks—the exact noise that panicked Raju.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The 3 Phases of a Major Trend
scenes.concept: The 3 Phases of a Major Trend

beatOutlines.textOutline: Tenet 3 states that every bull market unfolds in three phases: first is Accumulation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When everyone sells in despair, smart investors quietly accumulate. Then comes Public Participation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In Phase 3, Distribution, headlines scream euphoria while smart money offloads shares to the public.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

takeaways: The 3 Phases of a Major Trend

beatOutlines.textOutline: During Accumulation, the public sells in fear, but smart money absorbs all supply.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In Distribution, when retail traders buy excitedly at the top, smart money unloads onto them.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dow's fourth tenet is critical: the averages must confirm each other.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If factories make goods but transport falls, goods aren't shipping—a major warning sign.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Tenet 5 states: volume must confirm the trend—expanding in the primary direction.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And Tenet 6 is vital: a trend remains in effect until it gives a definite reversal signal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn. Read this scenario carefully and think.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: It is a Secondary correction inside a Primary bull market: 4 weeks long, 33% retracement, and low volume.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju realizes his mistake: he ignored the tide and traded a tiny ripple.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji smiles: until the secondary low breaks on heavy volume, the primary trend is your friend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Here are the key takeaways from today's chapter: from Charles Dow to the six basic tenets.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember: ride the primary ocean tide, prepare for secondary waves, and never fear minor ripples.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1884: Charles Dow created Industrial & Rail averages as an economic barometer
Tenet 1: The averages discount everything known or foreseeable
Tenet 2: Three trends — Tide (>1 yr), Wave (3 wks–3 mos, 33%–66%), Ripple (<3 wks)
Tenet 3: Three phases — Accumulation, Public Participation, Distribution
Tenet 4: Industrial & Transportation averages must confirm each other
Tenet 5: Volume must expand in the direction of the primary trend
Tenet 6: A trend remains intact until a definitive reversal signal occurs
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
